key_insight: Machine learning and multi-omics identified cytokine signatures associated with ICI myocarditis, with JAK–STAT signaling emerging across cohorts and amplified in CHIP carriers.
clinical_relevance: These findings suggest research targets for cytokine-guided risk stratification and pathway-directed treatment, but do not establish clinical utility or treatment benefit.
method: Machine learning and explainable AI analyzed cytokine profiles from patients receiving ICIs.
Single-cell multi-omics mapped implicated pathways and immune-cell contributions across three cohorts.
Stanford CyTOF data were used to validate Yale proteomic analyses.
evidence_signal: The study enrolled 236 cardio-oncology patients, including 88 receiving ICIs, and evaluated single-cell data from Yale (n=19), Stanford (n=25), and MGH (n=63).
watch_item: The abstract reports associations but no predictive performance metrics or prospective evidence that cytokine-guided care improves outcomes.
paper_title: Cytokine Signatures of Immune Checkpoint Inhibitor Myocarditis and the Modifying Role of Clonal Hematopoiesis: A Machine-Learning and Multi-Omics Study
